english.title: Receive instruction / training for terrorism - Terrorism Act 2006
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) received instruction or training in **(..SPECIFY THE SKILLS..), being skills mentioned in section 6(3) of the Terrorism Act 2006 and at the time of the instruction or training you intended to use the skills in which you were instructed or trained, for or in connection with the commission or preparation of acts of terrorism or Convention offences or for assisting the commission or preparation by others of such acts or offences
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6(2) and (5) of the Terrorism Act 2006.

english.notes:
(i) Section 6(3) of the Terrorism Act 2006 lists the following skills:
(a) the making, handling or use of a noxious substance, or of substances of a description of such substances;
(b) the use of any method or technique for doing anything else that is capable of being done for the purposes of terrorism, in connection with the commission or preparation of an act of terrorism or Convention offence or in connection with assisting the commission or preparation by another of such an act or offence; and
(c) the design or adaptation for the purposes of terrorism, or in connection with the commission or preparation of an act of terrorism or Convention offence, of any method or technique for doing anything.
(ii)Section 6(7) of the Act provides the interpretation of substance and noxious substance.
(iii) Also consider the offences of attendance at a place used for terrorist training (H8459) and offences regarding weapons training (H3785, H3786 and H 3787).
(iv) This offence applies to acts done outside the United Kingdom regardless of the nationality of the offender, see section 17 of the Act.
(v) For the liability of company directors etc. see section 18 of the Act.
(vi) Proceedings for this offence require the consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions, section 19 of the Act.
(vii) Section 7 of the Act provides for forfeiture powers for anything that has been in the person's possession for purposes connected with this offence.
(viii) See also Home Office Circular 8/2006 , including explanations about this section.
(ix) From 13th April 2015, the maximum sentence was amended from 10 years imprisonment to life imprisonment. This amendment applies only in relation to an offence committed on or after 13th April 2015. Where an offence is found to have been committed over a period of 2 or more days, or at some time during a period of 2 or more days, it must be taken to have been committed on the last of those days.

other.powersofarrest:
For terrorist offences primarily consider: Arrest without warrant - terrorism
Also applicable: Arrest without warrant
other.penalty:
Summary: Imprisonment for a term not exceeding twelve months and/or a fine.
Indictment: Life imprisonment and / or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

Notes
(i) In relation to an offence committed before paragraph 24(2) of Schedule 22 to the Sentencing Act 2020 comes into force, the reference to 12 months imprisonment in relation to summary offences, above, is to be read as a reference to 6 months imprisonment.
(ii) On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
(iii) This offence is also specified as a serious terrorism offence (Part 1 of Schedule 17A to the Sentencing Act 2020) and subject to serious terrorism sentences of imprisonment or extended sentences; see note (v) in section 306 for details.
